text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High GPU queue growth in prod - autoscaler not reacting (metric pipeline errors). Paging infra-oncall.

infra-oncall: got the page, joining. seeing cluster gpu usage at ~98% and queues stacking, HPA shows 0-> max no change. 

sre_jess: I'm on it, looking at HPA + adapter. Initial glance: prometheus-adapter logs showing timeouts and 503s to prometheus. metrics-server seems OK.

mlops_raj: confirmed increased inference queue length metric 'inference_queue_len' up from 200 to >1200 over 10m. throttling kicking in, customers seeing 429/503. Any quick mitigation?

prod_support_emily: we're getting a spike in support tickets and a couple of enterprise customers reported elevated latency and dropped requests. ETA on mitigation?

eng_lead_mike: prioritize mitigation first: reduce non-critical traffic, scale manually if needed. Also want root cause but handle the blast radius.

infra-oncall: quick checks:
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod
NAME                      REFERENCE                   TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-autoscaler      Deployment/inference-runtime  <unknown>/100%   2         50        2
```
HPA shows <unknown> because adapter failing to serve metrics.

sre_jess: that lines up. Prometheus-adapter returning 500/timeout for the custom metric queries. Checking adapter logs.

prometheus-bot: Alert: prometheus-adapter_k8s_error  (5xx rate increased)

sre_jess: adapter log snippet: 
```
E0314 12:05:12.345 adapter.go:241] error querying prometheus: context deadline exceeded
E0314 12:05:12.348 adapter.go:267] failed to convert series to metrics: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing"
```
Looks like connection to prometheus is flaky. Could be scrape backlog or OOM on prometheus.

mlops_raj: quick mitigation options:
- manually scale inference runtime deployment replicas to drain queues faster
- bump a temporary node pool with GPUs (if cloud supports)
- turn on tenant-level throttles to protect high-SLA customers
Which should we do first?

infra-oncall: I'm going to manually scale replicas to relieve queue while we fix adapter. Doing: `kubectl scale deploy inference-runtime -n prod --replicas=12`

deploy-bot: @infra-oncall performed: kubectl scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas=12 -n prod (revision 2026-03-14T12:06:01Z)

prod_support_emily: noting to customers: posting status update to status.redwood.ai — drafting message and will coordinate with customer_success_nina.

customer_success_nina: preparing targeted messages for impacted enterprise customers. Will attach temporary mitigation notes.

sre_jess: while replicas are coming up, I'm going to restart prometheus-adapter to re-establish metrics serving. Rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter -n monitoring`

infra-oncall: initiated restart.

prometheus-bot: prometheus-adapter pod/adapter-754c restarted at 12:09:05Z

sre_jess: after restart, adapter started returning metrics but with high latency. HPA now sees metrics but scaling is constrained by cluster capacity and GPU pod scheduling. Node autoscaler not kicking because metrics-server still shows nodes as available? Investigating node pool quota.

mlops_raj: we have a quota cap on GPU nodepools (cost control) that prevented node pool autoscaler from provisioning more GPUs. I can temporarily increase quota and request +2 nodes: `gcloud container clusters update redwood-prod --node-pool gpu-pool --max-nodes 10` (cloudcmd)

eng_lead_mike: approve temporary quota bump for incident window. Keep it limited and track cost.

infra-oncall: applied node-pool max increase, requesting scale. New nodes provisioning.

sre_jess: another issue: Prometheus itself had a remote_write backlog and was rejecting some queries from adapter due to resource exhaustion. Looking at Prometheus pods memory: one pod OOMKilled earlier. Investigating retention/ingesters.

prometheus-bot: Alert: prometheus_pod_restarts increased (monitoring/prometheus-0 restarted at 12:02)

mlops_raj: lowering scrape frequency temporarily for noisy exporters to reduce load: editing scrape_config for infra metrics (prod exporters) to 60s -> 120s for the duration. Applying patch.

infra-oncall: applied scrape interval changes. Prometheus memory pressure dropping. Adapter latency improving.

sre_jess: HPA now reporting proper metrics and scaling observed. HPA replicas increased from 2 -> 10 over ~5m. The manual scale to 12 and HPA are together stabilizing queue.

infra-oncall: queue length trending down from 1200 -> 260 over 18m. Throttles reduced. Customer-facing errors decreased.

prod_support_emily: support ticket rate back to baseline, customers updated. We'll leave status page note explaining root cause: metrics pipeline lag + prometheus OOM causing delayed autoscaling and GPU exhaustion.

eng_lead_mike: action items postmortem candidates:
- investigate Prometheus retention & resource sizing for metrics-adapter queries
- add circuit breaker between adapter and prometheus, limit concurrency
- implement emergency autoscale policy that bypasses adapter when HPA metrics unknown (fallback to queue-length via internal endpoint)
- automate temporary GPU capacity bump playbook for incidents
- add runbook steps to toggle non-critical tenant throttles

sre_jess: logging these items. I'll create an incident postmortem with timeline and root cause. Assigning follow-ups: prometheus scaling to mlops_raj, autoscale fallback to infra-oncall/eng_lead_mike, runbook updates to prod_support_emily.

customer_success_nina: closing loop with impacted customers, will send follow-up once postmortem is published.

infra-oncall: handing off oncall to sre_jess for next 2 hours while I grab lunch. Leaving notes in the incident doc.

sre_jess: taking handoff, monitoring the queue for 30m. Please ping if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to "mitigated" at 12:25Z; continued monitoring recommended.

mlops_raj: final check: average inference latency returned to normal band, and token serving velocity matches pre-incident numbers. I'll clean up temporary quota bump after 1 hour.

prod_support_emily: posting final status update and closing the incident channel for now. Thanks everyone for fast action. :clap:
